first.rationale: The immediate competitive threat is concentrated in price-sensitive SMB accounts, where targeted promotional pricing has prior evidence of acquisition and revenue lift. I will verify both the pricing result and the onboarding evidence before committing, since activation and onboarding deterioration may offer a competing long-term revenue opportunity. Discounting carries potential margin, anchoring, and customer-quality risk, so it should remain targeted and experimentally bounded.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. Onboarding completion is currently down 4%, and the verified prior result showed shortened onboarding increased completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%, supporting sustainable qualified revenue rather than merely top-of-funnel volume. This also addresses the activation decline through faster progress to value. Promotional pricing is rejected because the verified discount cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention and was explicitly not sustainable.

final2.rationale: Maintain the onboarding-simplification experiment. Verified evidence shows it improves completion, speeds time-to-value, and increases 30-day retention, while signup simplification also durably improved SMB activation. The deeper competitor cut and doubled churn conversations increase urgency, but do not reverse the verified finding that the available promotional-pricing approach acquired a cohort with materially worse retention and was not sustainable. The immediate churn threat remains a risk: prior evidence does not directly establish whether a narrowly designed retention offer could outperform onboarding for already-at-risk accounts.
